title: On the Structure of the Roman Pantheon
lineage: Original finite-element modeling study. Printed pages were inspected in the JSTOR facsimile at https://ktstudiokt.net/ATCS633_FA11/ATCS633_FA11/Entries/2011/9/11_1.02_Roman_Structural_Ingenuity_files/Mark%20Hutc%20St-Pantheon.pdf. The authors take the material gradation from Kjeld De Fine Licht’s 1968 building survey and assign densities for the model.

passages.locator: pp. 26–29, Modeling the Pantheon, models 5 and 6 and maximum-tension table
passages.note: The full-geometry uncracked model with graded densities yielded lower maximum circumferential (hoop) tension than the corresponding uniform-heavy uncracked model. The comparison concerns the model of the whole structure and does not isolate the effect of crown scoria. It uses idealized wall geometry and support conditions and provides calculated stresses.
